references.text: Repeats the counting of the tribe of Manasseh with the same number (32,200) when the camp arrangement is described.
The second census of the tribe of Manasseh, showing a significant increase to 52,700 men after 40 years in the wilderness.
Describes the birth of Manasseh as Joseph's firstborn son in Egypt and explains the origin of the tribe.
Jacob adopts Manasseh and Ephraim as his own sons, giving them status as separate tribes in Israel.
Jacob's blessing over Manasseh, where he prophesied that Manasseh would become a great people, but smaller than Ephraim.
